=============== axis-min-max-nullable ===============
title: 'fix(type): add missing nullable type for the axis `min` and `max` option'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript users can return `null` or `undefined` from axis `min` and `max` callbacks at runtime, but the current type declarations incorrectly reject that documented pattern.

  ## Desired outcome

  The type surface for axis `min` and `max` should allow nullable callback results so the declarations match the supported API.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Axis configurations whose `min` or `max` callbacks return `null` or `undefined` pass type-checking without changing the existing runtime behavior.

  '
=============== axislabel-formatter-index ===============
title: 'feat(axis): axisLabel `formatter` can receive its index for working with `customValues`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Axis label callbacks can format the label value, but authors working with `customValues` also need to know which generated tick they are formatting in order to line up external labels correctly.

  ## Desired outcome

  `axisLabel.formatter` should receive the tick index as an additional argument so formatter logic can work reliably with `customValues`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A formatter declared as `axisLabel.formatter(value, index)` receives the expected index for each displayed custom tick and can build labels from that position information.

  '
=============== axislabel-formatter-indexing ===============
title: 'fix(axis): refactor axisLabel formatter'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using custom axis label values needs labels to stay aligned with the same ordinal position they supplied, even when some custom values are filtered out because they fall outside the visible axis extent. Right now the formatter callback can receive the wrong index for repeated values because the label-building path looks the position back up from the filtered tick list instead of preserving the mapped position directly.


  ## Desired outcome

  When ECharts builds axis labels from `axisLabel.customValues`, the formatter should be called with the actual index of each rendered item in that filtered label sequence, including cases where the same numeric value appears more than once. Authors should be able to rely on formatter logic that branches on the index parameter without seeing duplicated values collapse onto the first matching position.


  ## Acceptance signals

  For duplicate or repeated custom label values that remain in range, each rendered label keeps its own formatter index and produces the text a user would expect from its own slot in the sequence. Existing axis label rendering behavior, formatter signatures, and label text generation outside this indexing bug remain unchanged.

title: 'feat(gauge): `progress.color` supports `''auto''`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Gauge authors can already let some visuals inherit the series color automatically, but progress arcs still require manual color duplication, which makes themed gauges harder to maintain.

  ## Desired outcome

  Gauge progress should accept `progress.color: ''auto''` so the progress fill can follow the series color mapping automatically.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When `progress.color` is set to `''auto''`, the gauge progress arc adopts the expected automatic color instead of requiring an explicit hard-coded fill.

  '
=============== graph-nodescaleratio-type ===============
title: 'fix(type): fix `nodeScaleRatio` option type for graph series'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The TypeScript declaration for graph `nodeScaleRatio` is narrower than the runtime behavior, so valid numeric configurations appear illegal in editors and build checks.

  ## Desired outcome

  The public type for `nodeScaleRatio` should accept the numeric values the runtime already supports rather than implying a single fixed literal.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Developers can provide ordinary numeric `nodeScaleRatio` values without TypeScript errors, and the runtime behavior remains unchanged.

  '
=============== jitter-overlap-avoidance ===============
title: 'fix(jitter): fix overlap when there is enough space to avoid'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors using scatter jitter are still seeing points overlap even when there is enough open space within the allowed jitter band, which makes dense plots look incorrect and undermines the point of enabling jitter in the first place.

  ## Desired outcome

  When overlap avoidance is enabled, the jitter placement should consistently choose a non-overlapping position whenever a valid position exists inside the permitted movement range, and it should only fall back when the available space is genuinely exhausted.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A scatter plot with nearby points no longer leaves avoidable collisions behind, and the adjusted points stay within the same jitter budget instead of jumping randomly while free space still exists.

  '
=============== label-layout-margin ===============
title: Fix/label layout margin
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors are hitting inconsistent label spacing and overlap behavior across pie charts and shared label layout code, especially around margins, stroke-aware bounds, and post-layout updates.

  ## Desired outcome

  Label layout should apply the same geometry rules everywhere so `minMargin`, `textMargin`, hidden-overlap handling, and final label bounds behave consistently after layout adjustments.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Labels keep the intended spacing, pie labels and shared axis labels no longer drift because of inconsistent margin math, and overlap prevention reflects the final rendered label geometry.

  '
=============== labelline-smooth-reset ===============
title: 'fix(label): fix labelLine `smooth` can not be reset'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pie labels can keep a stale curved guide line after `labelLine.smooth` is turned off or reset to zero, so option updates do not faithfully reflect the current configuration.

  ## Desired outcome

  Changing `labelLine.smooth` back to `false` or `0` should fully reset the guide line to a straight path instead of preserving the previous smoothing.

  ## Acceptance signals

  After updating `labelLine.smooth`, the rendered label line immediately matches the new setting and does not retain an old smooth curve.

  '

title: 'fix(line): fix areaStyle render error when dimension name is empty string'
category: bugfix

  ## Desired outcome

  Area rendering should tolerate empty-string dimension names instead of treating them as a fatal path through the line-series logic.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A line chart with `areaStyle` and a dataset dimension named `''''` renders normally instead of failing during area generation.

  '
=============== lines-loop-symbol-flip ===============
title: 'fix(lines): fix effect symbol flip on unidirectional loop end when `roundTrip` is not enabled'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Animated symbols on one-way looping `lines` series can briefly flip direction when they cross the loop endpoint, which makes the motion look glitchy even though the route itself is correct.

  ## Desired outcome

  When `roundTrip` is not enabled, the effect symbol should preserve a consistent forward orientation across the loop boundary instead of flipping at the turnaround point.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A unidirectional looping line animation remains visually continuous, with the effect symbol keeping the expected orientation as it passes the loop end.

  '
=============== logscale-negative-exponent-rounding ===============
title: 'fix(logScale): Fix incorrect rounding usage, and support data with big negative exponent.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  ## Desired outcome

  Log-scale rounding should handle extremely small values consistently so charts with tiny magnitudes remain numerically correct and readable.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A log axis fed with very small values no longer mis-rounds its scale, and the resulting ticks and labels stay stable across the supported exponent range.

  '

category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors can control stacking depth for many series elements, but marker overlays still lack the same control, which makes it difficult to layer annotations correctly over complex charts.

  ## Desired outcome

  `markPoint`, `markLine`, and `markArea` should accept a `z` option so authors can place marker overlays at the intended rendering depth without relying on brittle layering hacks.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When a marker is given an explicit `z`, it renders above or below neighboring content in the same predictable way users expect from other chart elements.

  '

title: 'fix(matrix): fix darkMode color'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Matrix charts in dark mode still use colors that were tuned for light backgrounds, so borders and structural surfaces can become hard to distinguish and the component looks visually broken next to the rest of the dark theme.

  ## Desired outcome

  The dark theme should provide matrix-specific colors that keep the matrix body, dividers, and borders legible and visually balanced on dark backgrounds.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A matrix rendered with dark mode shows clear separation between cells and surrounding structure, without washed-out or light-theme border colors leaking through.

  '

title: 'feat(matrix): support matrix.x/y.length for conveniently creating a headless matrix without composing an array'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Creating a headless matrix currently requires authors to build explicit coordinate arrays even when they only know the desired matrix dimensions, which adds unnecessary setup overhead.

  ## Desired outcome

  Matrix definitions should allow `matrix.x.length` and `matrix.y.length` so users can declare the size of a headless matrix directly without composing placeholder arrays.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A matrix configured only with dimension lengths produces the expected headless grid structure, while existing array-based matrix definitions continue to work.

  '

title: Fix matrix label API
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Matrix users are seeing inconsistent label behavior because matrix labels do not reliably inherit shared text defaults, and coordinate locator ranges can become invalid in edge cases.

  ## Desired outcome

  Matrix labels should inherit `option.textStyle` the same way other labels do, and matrix coordinate lookup should handle invalid locator ranges predictably, including the `coordClamp` path instead of producing unusable results.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Matrix labels pick up the expected default text styling, and matrix coordinate calculations no longer fail or return confusing ranges when some locator values are missing or out of bounds.

  '

title: 'fix(matrix): fix matrix label formatter does not work'
category: bugfix

  ## Desired outcome

  Matrix labels should honor `label.formatter` consistently, including string templates and function formatters, and formatter callbacks should receive the expected matrix label context such as `name`, `value`, and `coord`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A matrix label configured with either formatter style renders the formatted text rather than the raw value, and callback formatters receive the documented data they need.

  '

  ## Desired outcome

  ## Acceptance signals

  When later series contain values outside the first series’ bounds, the parallel axis expands correctly instead of truncating the data.

  '

  ## Desired outcome

  ## Acceptance signals

  '

  '

title: 'fix(toolbox): fix dataView component does not fit dark mode'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The toolbox data view still looks like a light-theme popup when the rest of the chart is in dark mode, making the editor hard to read and visually out of place.

  ## Desired outcome

  Dark mode should style the data view surface, text, textarea, and controls coherently so the toolbox editor feels native to the dark theme.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Opening `toolbox.feature.dataView` in dark mode shows readable text and controls on an appropriate dark background instead of a mismatched light popup.

  '
=============== toolbox-emphasis-color ===============
title: 'fix(toolbox): fix emphasis color to be different with default color'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The toolbox hover state is not visually distinct enough because the emphasis color can collapse to the default icon color, making interaction feedback easy to miss.

  ## Desired outcome

  Toolbox emphasis styling should use a different highlight color so hover and focus states are visibly distinguishable from the default icon appearance.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When the toolbox enters emphasis state, `emphasis.iconStyle.borderColor` produces a clearly different visual highlight instead of matching the normal icon color.

  '
=============== tooltip-listener-unbinding ===============
title: 'fix(tooltip): fix potential memory leakage by explicitly unbinding event listeners'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Applications that repeatedly create and dispose tooltip-heavy charts can accumulate leftover DOM listeners, which is the kind of slow memory growth that operators only notice after long sessions or repeated route changes.

  ## Desired outcome

  Disposing or rebuilding chart tooltips should fully release the HTML tooltip event wiring so long-lived pages do not retain stale listeners or detached tooltip state.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Repeated chart teardown and recreation no longer leaves tooltip listeners behind, and tooltip behavior remains correct without introducing leaks over time.

  '
=============== typescript-esm-compatibility ===============
title: 'fix(types): remove export assignment to support typescript esm compatibility'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript consumers using modern ESM resolution are running into friction with the published declaration entrypoints, especially in projects that mix `import` and `require` semantics.

  ## Desired outcome

  The published package should expose type entrypoints that work cleanly for modern TypeScript module resolution, including distinct ESM and CommonJS declaration paths where needed.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Projects using current TypeScript ESM rules can resolve the package’s declarations without manual hacks, and mixed consumers still receive the correct type surface for their module mode.

  '
=============== typescript-export-types ===============
title: 'fix(type): fix missing or missmatched TS export types'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript consumers are running into missing or mismatched exported option types, especially for series that combine shared coordinate-system mixins, which makes valid configurations look unsupported in editor tooling.

  ## Desired outcome

  The published TypeScript surface should export the correct option types for affected series and include the calendar and matrix mixins where those series actually support them.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Developers importing the affected series option types no longer see missing exports or incomplete coordinate-system support in TypeScript, and valid options type-check as expected.

  '
=============== typo-cleanup ===============
title: 'chore: fix typos'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The project has accumulated a handful of spelling mistakes and mislabeled identifiers in internal code and example data, which makes maintenance harder and leaves contributors second-guessing whether a name is intentional.

  ## Desired outcome

  Clean up the wording and identifier typos so the codebase reads consistently, while keeping existing runtime behavior, public API contracts, and chart output unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Contributors see corrected names and messages in the affected areas, and no chart behavior or user-facing option semantics change as a side effect of the cleanup.

  '
=============== visualmap-darkmode-inrange ===============
title: 'fix(visualMap): fix dark mode should not provide inRange'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  In dark mode, visualMap is still injecting default `inRange` colors, which can unexpectedly override the palette choices chart authors already configured for their own mappings.

  ## Desired outcome

  The dark theme should stop supplying a default `visualMap.inRange` color mapping so dark mode does not silently change how user-defined visual mapping behaves.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Enabling dark mode no longer adds an unwanted in-range color ramp, and visualMap styling follows the user’s own configuration unless they explicitly opt in to theme values.

  '
=============== visualmap-unbounded-range ===============
title: VisualMap support unboundedRange
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Continuous visual maps currently force both ends of `range` to behave as hard bounds, which makes it awkward to express common selections like “everything above this threshold” or “everything below this threshold.”

  ## Desired outcome

  Users should be able to mark one side of the selected interval as open-ended by enabling `visualMap.unboundedRange`, so the visual map can naturally represent one-sided ranges without custom workarounds.

  ## Acceptance signals

  With `visualMap.unboundedRange`, a range that touches the configured minimum or maximum behaves as an open interval on that side, while the opposite bound remains effective.

  '

    risk: { type: 'string', description: 'what could break, or unknowns remaining' },
  },
  required: ['slug', 'files', 'summary', 'confidence', 'risk'],
  additionalProperties: false,
}

function prompt(slug) {
  return `You are researching ONE change request for the Apache ECharts repository at /workspace (version 6.0.0-beta.1, TypeScript source under /workspace/src, unit tests under /workspace/test/ut/spec, visual test html under /workspace/test).

Your requirement slug is: **${slug}**
Read /workspace/requirements/${slug}.yaml first — it is the authoritative statement of what must change.

This repo is a real snapshot of apache/echarts just before a set of real upstream commits. Your job is to work out, from the actual source code, exactly what the fix/feature must be, at the level of concrete code edits.

RULES:

- Use Read/Grep/Glob/Bash(read-only) freely. Read the ACTUAL code — never guess at file contents or API shapes. Verify every symbol, option name, type name and file path you cite by opening the file.
- Search widely: src/, test/ut/spec/, test/*.html, index.d.ts, package.json, build/, theme/, ssr/, extension-src/. Related option types often live in src/component/**/[X]Model.ts, src/coord/**, src/util/types.ts, src/util/states.ts, src/label/*, src/scale/*.

DELIVERABLE: write a detailed implementation plan to /workspace/agent_plans/${slug}.md using the Write tool. It must contain, in markdown:
1. **Goal** — restate what must change, in engineering terms.
2. **Findings** — the exact current code that is wrong/missing, with \`path:line\` references and quoted snippets of the current code.
3. **Plan** — an ordered list of edits. For EACH edit give: the file path, the exact anchor (existing code to search for, quoted verbatim so it can be matched), and the exact replacement/new code, fully written out and compilable TypeScript matching surrounding style (4-space indent, existing import conventions, Apache license header on new files).

5. **Verification** — what command(s) prove it works (e.g. \`npx tsc --noEmit\`, \`npx jest --config test/ut/jest.config.cjs -t "..."\`).

Be exhaustive and concrete: another engineer must be able to apply your plan without re-deriving anything. If the requirement is vague, look for the smallest coherent real change that satisfies every acceptance signal in the yaml, and prefer touching the code paths the yaml names.

Finally return the structured summary object. \`files\` must list every repo file the plan will modify or create (excluding the plan file itself).`
}

log(`research complete: ${ok.length}/${SLUGS.length}`)
return ok
